newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovaks object to U.S. NATO enlargement report.
newsitem.headline: Slovaks object to U.S. NATO enlargement report.

text.p: Slovakia on Tuesday expressed concern over doubts cast on its respect for democracy and human rights in a U.S. report on NATO expansion.

A Slovak Foreign Ministry statement branded as "superficial" the conclusions of the report to Congress which noted what it said were serious problems over respect for human rights in some states, including Slovakia, seeking to join NATO.
NATO is due to announce names of countries to be invited to negotiate membership at a July summit in Madrid. The Czech Republic, Hungary and Poland are leading contenders.
Eleven former communist countries have expressed interest in joining and entered a dialogue with the alliance.
"Slovakia understands this dialogue as an effort to objectively and factually assess the real state of the Slovak Republic," the statement said.

"The foreign ministry in this sense studied in detail the report and is concerned by the manner in which it casts doubt on the respect for democratic norms and basic human rights in the Slovak Republic."
The U.S. report, presented on February 24, said that "serious problems have been noted in some (countries), such as Albania and Slovakia..." regarding respect for human rights.
One western diplomat said the ministry appeared stung by the mention together of Slovakia and Albania, where a state of emergency has been declared after violent unrest.

"We must state with regret that simplified and inappropriate comparisons of the situation in Slovakia with that in other parts of Europe are...inadequate with regard to what Slovakia has achieved on the path of transformation...and its active relationship towards NATO," the ministry said.
Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar's nationalist-populist coalition government has declared membership in NATO and the European Union are its top foreign policy priorities.
Meciar has repeatedly asserted he wants Slovakia to be among the first former Soviet bloc countries to join.

Slovakia was once considered to be among the top contenders, but its chances have waned as the United States and the European Union have repeatedly criticised Bratislava for lagging behind in democratic reform.
The Slovak parliament approved a resolution last month to hold a referendum on NATO membership.
